title: Spectral optimization of spherical lattices and applications to classical and quantum interacting spin systems
authors: Jonas Völler, Grigorios Makris, Fabian Hassler, Stefan Wessel
abstract: We develop an optimization algorithm for spherical lattice discretizations based on the spectrum of the discretized Laplace operator. Starting from refined icosahedral lattices, we minimize the splitting of the $(2\ell+1)$, $\ell=0,1,2,\dots$, continuum multiplets expected from $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ symmetry via gradient descent. This approach simultaneously produces lattices based on triangles with nearly uniform circumradii and perimeters. Although the optimization uses only the free-particle spectrum, we show that the resulting lattices carry over to interacting models. On the optimized lattices, rotational symmetry is restored for the critical Ising and Potts models and primary scaling dimensions are accurately reproduced for the three-dimensional Ising conformal field theory, when appropriate geometry-dependent interaction strengths are used. Higher-angular-momentum descendant states reveal weak residual symmetry breaking beyond the sectors protected by the underlying icosahedral symmetry.
summary: This work develops a spectral optimization algorithm to improve the geometry of spherical lattices by minimizing the splitting of energy levels derived from the Laplace operator. By optimizing the lattice structure, the authors successfully restore rotational symmetry for critical spin models like the Ising model. The findings emphasize that achieving continuum symmetry requires both geometrically optimized lattices and the correct critical interaction couplings.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of accurately discretizing continuous geometries, like the sphere, for physical models while minimizing the artificial breaking of underlying symmetries.
main_result: Spectral optimization of the lattice geometry successfully restores rotational symmetry for critical models like the Ising and Potts models, provided the lattice geometry is optimized alongside appropriate critical couplings.
method: A gradient descent algorithm is employed to minimize a loss function based on the spectral splitting of the free-particle Laplace operator's energy multiplets.
model_or_system: The study focuses on discretizing physical systems (Ising, Potts, TFIM) on the sphere using icosahedral lattices, modeled via a lattice Hamiltonian derived from the discretized Laplace operator.
key_observables:
Spectral splitting of energy multiplets (diagnosing SO(3) symmetry breaking), geometric uniformity measures ($
u_R, 
u_P$), and primary scaling dimensions for the 3D Ising CFT.
important_parameters: The optimization process is sensitive to the choice of couplings (e.g., constant vs. Laplacian) and the proximity to the critical point.
main_assumptions: The optimization process is assumed to transfer its success from the free-particle spectrum to the full interacting models, though residual symmetry breaking persists in higher-angular-momentum states.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the optimization process (Loss vs. Uniformity), compare symmetry breaking signals for different lattice orientations and coupling types, and show the temperature dependence of symmetry breaking.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the spectral diagnostic tool and the optimization method using gradient descent on the free-particle spectrum. It then applies this to restore symmetry in critical spin models, concluding that both optimized geometry and critical couplings are necessary for full symmetry recovery.
why_interesting: The rigorous connection between geometric optimization (minimizing spectral splitting) and the recovery of continuum symmetries in critical quantum field theories is highly relevant for developing accurate lattice simulations in quantum many-body physics.

figures.caption: Figure 1: Initialization of a spherical lattice starting from an icosahedral seed with a subdivision level of k = 3. (figure adapted from [3])

Figure 2: Construction of the Laplacian couplings. Left: the dual lattice, obtained by connecting the circumcenters (open circles) of neighboring triangles, encloses the Voronoi cell of vertex i (shaded blue). Right: the coupling Ji j is set by half the ratio of the shared dual edge length l∗ i j to the direct lattice edge length li j.

Figure 3: Energy spectrum of the free-particle Hamiltonian for base icosahedral lat- tices with N = 162 (left) and N = 642 (right) vertices. Both spectra exhibit the ex- pected continuum degeneracy only for ℓ≤2, which we indicate with green outlines. We furthermore indicate the first level with degeneracy splitting, corresponding to ℓ= 3, with red outlines. The labeling of the x-axis indicates the indexing of the en- ergy levels.

Figure 4: Energy spectrum of the free-particle Hamiltonian for optimized icosahedral lattices with N = 162 (left) and N = 642 (right) vertices. The degeneracy of levels with ℓ≤2 is still exact. Furthermore, the optimized lattices exhibit substantially improved degeneracy for higher angular momentum energy levels. The labeling of the x-axis again indicates the indexing of the energy levels.

Figure 5: Movement of the vertices during optimization. Left: the background shows the base icosahedral lattice. Blue arrows indicate where vertices will end up after optimizing. The arrows are only shown for one of the original 20 faces. The three vertices of the original regular icosahedron enclosing that face are indicated with white open circles. Right: sketch of how the optimization evens out the non-uniform projection of the initial lattice construction.
